Second, figures/FIG-4.md now gives the ordered contactor shedding step 210 a line leaving its left side that runs leftward clear of every rectangle and joins the return line to the available-charging-current determination step 200, so the sheet shows the outcome paragraph 51 describes, where a branch current that has fallen within the verification interval returns the process to allocation without passing through the reclose permissive step 212. Adding geometry to FIG. 2 took it past the 2800-character ceiling, so I recovered the space inside that file by tightening wording only, and it now stands at 2798 characters with the same seven numerals. The two failing mechanical gates, every specification numeral appearing in a drawing and each described figure having a sheet, both depend on rendered images. figures/ still holds four Markdown briefs and no rendered sheet, review/figure-audit-evidence.json still does not exist, and producing image files is outside what I can do here, so those gates close when the drawing pass renders these four briefs and regenerates the evidence. Claims, numerals.md, drawing descriptions and the FIG. 1 and FIG. 3 briefs are unchanged. As input/brief.md records, no prior-art search was run and prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so the art backdrop may be incomplete.
reasoning: The bus finding was worth taking seriously because the source is specific about what shares that bus: the controller communicates with the connector interfaces and the contactors over it. Routing the sensor channel onto the same bus was an inference I had drawn, not a disclosed fact, and once drawn it was doing real work on the page, since an isolated bus that also carries the measurement path reads as a different architecture from one that does not. Removing the assertion costs the invention nothing, because the disclosed requirement is only that the controller verify connector current with the corresponding sensor, which the neutral coupling sentence states without choosing a path.

In FIG. 2 I gave the first connector current sensor 122 a separate unqualified line rather than deleting its connection. A sensor drawn with no outgoing path would contradict the description, which has the controller obtaining its evidence of drawn current from that sensor. The line leaves through the right part of the lower side so that it is distinguishable from the bus, which rises into the rectangle further left, and no character of it is described as the bus.

The FIG. 4 finding was a real mismatch between sheet and text, not a rendering artifact. The description gives step 210 two outcomes, and the brief drew only one, so every path through the protection sequence ran through the reclose permissive step 212, which paragraph 59 confines to a contactor actually opened by shedding. The new line restores the second outcome and merges into the existing return, so the sheet still has one arrowhead into the available-charging-current determination step 200 rather than a second entry point to reconcile.

I fixed this in the brief rather than by trimming the description, because the description is the higher authority and its two-outcome statement traces directly to the source sentence about opening contactors only if branch current remains above the branch limit after the reduced pilot command and the verification interval.

The character ceiling forced trimming in FIG. 2, and I spent it on wording only: shorter connectives, a possessive in place of a prepositional phrase, and merging one identifying clause into its placement sentence. Every disclosed relationship survived, including both power-path devices straddling the same path, the pilot interface tied to the connector, the bus reaching the pilot interface and the contactor, and the left run of the bus lying outside the rectangle's horizontal span, which is the wording that fixed the earlier leader failure.

content:
The current draft did not pass the automatic filing gate.

Read review/previous-qa.md, then fix every listed mechanical check and every independently
verified finding. Do not argue with a finding in the structured response. If wording triggered a
false positive, make the draft unambiguous enough that the check passes without changing the
invention. Keep the reference-numeral table, drawing descriptions, detailed description, claims,
and every file in figures/ synchronized.

Generated pixels are never authority for the invention. The authority order is the inventor's
disclosure and conversation, then the patent text, then the figure briefs, then the rendered
sheets. Never change the claims, description, numeral table, or disclosed embodiments merely to
excuse geometry, an object, or a leader endpoint that the image model drew incorrectly. Never add
an implementation detail or embodiment because it appeared in a generated image. For a drawing
finding, preserve the authoritative invention, strengthen the figure brief, and regenerate the
sheet from the authoritative text until the pixels conform. A stubborn rendering artifact remains
a drawing defect; it does not become part of the invention.

For a figure-plan coverage failure, never delete a disclosed part, numeral definition, or
supporting specification text. Redistribute labels among focused sheets, or add a focused sheet
when necessary, and synchronize the drawing descriptions.

If a figure brief is over-specified, shorten it by removing invented rendering constraints while
preserving the authoritative text, numeral table, disclosed geometry, and required relationships.
Replace generic negative linework controls with positive descriptions of the required bodies,
edges, contacts, openings, and paths. Do not ban second boundaries, parallel lines, inner lines,
rims, ledges, or chamfers merely to suppress a prior rendering artifact.
Remove generic face-linework controls such as prescribing one stroke for every outline or a
shared edge drawn once. Keep only the positive physical geometry and relationship.
For an endpoint finding, choose a broad interior target on the intended part whenever possible.
Remove exact midpoint, depth, quarter, or toward-an-end modifiers that are not disclosure-grounded
or necessary to distinguish the intended part. Replace ordinal geometry references with explicit
outermost, middle, innermost, left, or right terms whenever the order could be read in more than
one direction.

Leave no note, placeholder, question, or instruction for a person. Return the structured answer
with `action` set to "revised" and `questions` as an empty array.

In figures/FIG-1.md the endpoints for the branch conductor 102 and the isolated local bus 106 are now stated separately: the branch conductor leader ends on that line clear of any junction and clear of the small open rectangle straddling it, which keeps it off the branch current sensor 104, and the bus leader ends on the horizontal portion of that line clear of any junction and clear of the two short parallel strokes crossing it. Both files were trimmed only in wording to stay under the 2800-character ceiling, at 2712 and 2791 characters, and every disclosed body, path and relationship on both sheets is unchanged. No geometry was added, no negative linework control was written, and no numeral moved. FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 are untouched, as are the claims, draft/numerals.md, the drawing descriptions and the detailed description. All 23 numerals remain defined once each and listed on exactly one sheet, with 8, 7, 8 and 8 numerals per sheet. As input/brief.md records, no prior-art search was run and prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so the art backdrop may be incomplete.
reasoning: The critical and major findings are the same defect seen twice, and both are cured by rendering, which the reviewer's own suggested fix says requires no change to the specification, the numeral table or the drawing plan. So the useful work available to me was to remove the remaining places where a leader could legitimately land somewhere the check would reject, since a render that arrives and then fails inspection costs another full cycle.

FIG. 3 carried the exact wording that failed on FIG. 2 two rounds ago: end the leader on the portion of that line outside the enclosing rectangle. On this sheet the bus happens to run rightward from the rectangle, so the phrase was true, but it is measured by horizontal span and there was no reason to leave the same latent ambiguity standing. Stating it as a horizontal position to the right of the right side of the enclosing rectangle names the one condition the inspection measures.

On both FIG. 1 and FIG. 3 the branch conductor 102 shares its line with the small open rectangle of the branch current sensor 104 straddling it. Away from any junction did not exclude the sensor rectangle, so a leader for 102 could terminate on 104 and be scored as a misplaced numeral. Clear of the small open rectangle straddling it distinguishes the two parts, which is exactly the case where a placement constraint is warranted rather than aesthetic.

The isolated local bus 106 on FIG. 1 runs horizontally with two vertical branches and the isolation strokes crossing it, so I named those features to steer the leader away from them while keeping the target broad: any point on the horizontal run qualifies. I did not specify a fraction of the run, a distance, or a side, because none of that is disclosure-grounded and a narrow target is what produces retries.

Staying under the character ceiling came out of wording, not content: the no-shading phrase and the longer sentence about text and numerals. Every body, line, junction and schematic marking on both sheets survived, including the isolation strokes, which carry the disclosed fact that the bus is isolated between the controller and the connector stations.

I left FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 alone. Their endpoints already read positionally and the return path added last round matches the two outcomes the description gives step 210, so reopening them would risk a regression in files the reviewer now reports as consistent.

content.content:
Run the complete current filing gate against the existing application. Preserve the source-clean filing text unless an independent review identifies a real defect. Regenerate every stale or missing drawing sheet, verify exact figure and sheet numbering, every reference numeral, leader endpoint, OCR result, geometry relationship, and text-to-drawing relationship, and publish only after every filing blocker clears.
=== QA ===
# Previous review - verdict: fail

Source fidelity and internal consistency of the text are sound. Every claim limitation, every numbered part, and every process step in draft/08-detailed-description.md traces to an exact passage in input/disclosure.md (repeated verbatim in input/conversation.md): the branch limit below the sum of connector ratings; per-connector contactor, connector current sensor, control-pilot interface and local connector identifier; the upstream branch current sensor as an independent safety input; the isolated local bus; the four stored per-session values; the subtract-non-charging-load-and-safety-reserve arithmetic; minimum-sustaining-then-deficit distribution; pilot transmission with connector-sensor verification; the reduced-pilot / verification-interval / ordered-shedding ladder; the three-condition reclose permissive; welded-contactor recording with inhibit of the other contactors and the local fault indicator; the offline signed token, last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory and tamper-evident meter sequence; and the service-input mapping with store-only-on-agreement. I found no added structure, relationship, result, material or embodiment, no numeral that labels more than one part (100-136 and 200-214 are identical across the description, draft/numerals.md and the four briefs, and all 23 are used exactly as defined), no naming drift for the same element, and no statement in one section that contradicts another. The abstract is 142 words. The draft contains no [REF:] citation, which is correct: prior_art/ holds only INDEX.md, whose reference table is empty. As input/brief.md records that no prior-art search was run, the art backdrop available to this review is empty by design and may be incomplete. The defects are confined entirely to the drawing package: figures/ still contains only FIG-1.md through FIG-4.md and no rendered sheet exists for any figure, and review/figure-audit-evidence.json is absent, so no pixel, OCR, numeral-placement, leader or geometry verification was possible and both failing mechanical gates stand unresolved from the previous QA cycle.

What is claimed is:

1. A charging control system for a plurality of electric-vehicle connectors supplied by a common electrical branch, the system comprising:

a plurality of connector stations, each connector station of the plurality comprising a contactor connected between the electrical branch and a respective electric-vehicle connector of the plurality of electric-vehicle connectors, a connector current sensor arranged to measure a connector current of the respective electric-vehicle connector, and a control-pilot interface arranged to present an assigned limit to a vehicle coupled to the respective electric-vehicle connector;

a branch current sensor arranged to measure a branch current of the electrical branch upstream of the contactors of the plurality of connector stations;

an isolated local bus; and

a controller coupled to the plurality of connector stations over the isolated local bus and coupled to the branch current sensor, the controller configured to store a branch limit that is lower than a sum of ratings of the plurality of electric-vehicle connectors and to store, for each active connector of the plurality of electric-vehicle connectors, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current, and an energy-deficit value;

wherein the controller is configured to, at each allocation interval:

subtract, from the branch limit, a measured non-charging branch load of the electrical branch and a configurable safety reserve, to obtain an available charging current;

assign the minimum sustaining current to each session at an active connector that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distribute a remaining portion of the available charging current among the active connectors according to the energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining the assigned limit for each of the active connectors;

send each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface of the corresponding connector station; and

verify a resulting connector current of that connector station with the connector current sensor of that connector station; and

wherein the controller is further configured to send a reduced pilot command through the control-pilot interface of at least one connector station of the plurality and to start a verification interval, and, when a measured branch current from the branch current sensor remains above the branch limit after the reduced pilot command has been sent and the verification interval has elapsed, to open the contactors of the plurality of connector stations one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch limit.

2. The system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured not to reclose a contactor that has been opened in the stored shedding order until the connector current sensor of the connector station of that contactor reports zero connector current, the control-pilot interface of that connector station reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired.

3. The system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to record a welded-contactor condition for a connector station when the connector current measured by the connector current sensor of that connector station remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector station.

4. The system of claim 3, further comprising a local fault indicator, wherein the controller is configured, upon recording the welded-contactor condition, to inhibit the contactors of the other connector stations supplied by the electrical branch and to operate the local fault indicator.

5. The system of claim 1, further comprising a network interface and a nonvolatile memory, wherein the controller is configured to receive remote schedules and authorizations through the network interface, to store a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit in the nonvolatile memory, and, during a network outage, to continue already authorized sessions subject to the last accepted branch limit, to send the reduced pilot command, and, when the measured branch current from the branch current sensor remains above the last accepted branch limit after the reduced pilot command has been sent and the verification interval has elapsed, to open the contactors of the plurality of connector stations one at a time in the stored shedding order.

6. The system of claim 5, wherein the controller is configured not to start a session at a newly connected electric-vehicle connector during the network outage unless the signed local authorization token authorizes that electric-vehicle connector and has not expired.

7. The system of claim 5, wherein the controller is configured to append meter records to a tamper-evident local sequence and to upload the appended meter records through the network interface when communication returns.

8. The system of claim 1, further comprising a service input, wherein the controller is configured, in response to the service input, to associate local connector identifiers with the contactors of the plurality of connector stations by commanding one low-energy pilot transition at a time through the control-pilot interface of a commanded connector station and confirming a response at the connector current sensor of that connector station, and to store an association between a local connector identifier and a contactor only after the connector current sensor that responds to the commanded low-energy pilot transition agrees with the commanded connector station.

9. A method of controlling charging at a plurality of electric-vehicle connectors supplied by a common electrical branch having a branch limit that is lower than a sum of ratings of the plurality of electric-vehicle connectors, each electric-vehicle connector of the plurality being served by a contactor, by a connector current sensor, and by a control-pilot interface, and the electrical branch having a branch current sensor upstream of the contactors, the method comprising:

storing, for each active connector of the plurality of electric-vehicle connectors, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current, and an energy-deficit value;

at each allocation interval, subtracting from the branch limit a measured non-charging branch load of the electrical branch and a configurable safety reserve, to obtain an available charging current;

assigning the minimum sustaining current to each session at an active connector that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distributing a remaining portion of the available charging current among the active connectors according to the energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned limit for each of the active connectors;

sending each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface of the corresponding electric-vehicle connector and verifying a resulting connector current with the connector current sensor of that electric-vehicle connector;

sending a reduced pilot command through the control-pilot interface of at least one of the electric-vehicle connectors and starting a verification interval; and

when a measured branch current from the branch current sensor remains above the branch limit after the reduced pilot command has been sent and the verification interval has elapsed, opening the contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch limit.

10. The method of claim 9, further comprising withholding reclosure of a contactor opened in the stored shedding order until the connector current sensor of the electric-vehicle connector of that contactor reports zero connector current, the control-pilot interface of that electric-vehicle connector reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired.

11. The method of claim 9, further comprising recording a welded-contactor condition for an electric-vehicle connector when the connector current measured by the connector current sensor of that electric-vehicle connector remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that electric-vehicle connector, and, upon recording the welded-contactor condition, inhibiting the contactors of the other electric-vehicle connectors supplied by the electrical branch and operating a local fault indicator.

12. The method of claim 9, further comprising storing a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit in a nonvolatile memory, and, during a network outage, continuing already authorized sessions subject to the last accepted branch limit and declining to start a session at a newly connected electric-vehicle connector unless the signed local authorization token authorizes that electric-vehicle connector and has not expired.

What is claimed is:

1. A charging control system for a plurality of electric-vehicle connectors supplied by a common electrical branch, the system comprising:

a plurality of connector stations, each connector station of the plurality comprising a contactor connected between the electrical branch and a respective electric-vehicle connector of the plurality of electric-vehicle connectors, a connector current sensor arranged to measure a connector current of the respective electric-vehicle connector, and a control-pilot interface arranged to present an assigned limit to a vehicle coupled to the respective electric-vehicle connector;

a branch current sensor arranged to measure a branch current of the electrical branch upstream of the contactors of the plurality of connector stations;

an isolated local bus; and

a controller coupled to the plurality of connector stations over the isolated local bus and coupled to the branch current sensor, the controller configured to store a branch limit that is lower than a sum of ratings of the plurality of electric-vehicle connectors and to store, for each active connector of the plurality of electric-vehicle connectors, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current, and an energy-deficit value;

wherein the controller is configured to, at each allocation interval:

subtract, from the branch limit, a measured non-charging branch load of the electrical branch and a configurable safety reserve, to obtain an available charging current;

assign the minimum sustaining current to each session at an active connector that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distribute a remaining portion of the available charging current among the active connectors according to the energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining the assigned limit for each of the active connectors;

send each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface of the corresponding connector station; and

verify a resulting connector current of that connector station with the connector current sensor of that connector station; and

wherein the controller is further configured to send a reduced pilot command through the control-pilot interface of at least one connector station of the plurality and to start a verification interval, and, when a measured branch current from the branch current sensor remains above the branch limit after the reduced pilot command has been sent and the verification interval has elapsed, to open the contactors of the plurality of connector stations one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch limit.

2. The system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured not to reclose a contactor that has been opened in the stored shedding order until the connector current sensor of the connector station of that contactor reports zero connector current, the control-pilot interface of that connector station reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired.

3. The system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to record a welded-contactor condition for a connector station when the connector current measured by the connector current sensor of that connector station remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector station.

4. The system of claim 3, further comprising a local fault indicator, wherein the controller is configured, upon recording the welded-contactor condition, to inhibit the contactors of the other connector stations supplied by the electrical branch and to operate the local fault indicator.

5. The system of claim 1, further comprising a network interface and a nonvolatile memory, wherein the controller is configured to receive remote schedules and authorizations through the network interface, to store a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit in the nonvolatile memory, and, during a network outage, to continue already authorized sessions subject to the last accepted branch limit, to send the reduced pilot command, and, when the measured branch current from the branch current sensor remains above the last accepted branch limit after the reduced pilot command has been sent and the verification interval has elapsed, to open the contactors of the plurality of connector stations one at a time in the stored shedding order.

6. The system of claim 5, wherein the controller is configured not to start a session at a newly connected electric-vehicle connector during the network outage unless the signed local authorization token authorizes that electric-vehicle connector and has not expired.

7. The system of claim 5, wherein the controller is configured to append meter records to a tamper-evident local sequence and to upload the appended meter records through the network interface when communication returns.

8. The system of claim 1, further comprising a service input, wherein the controller is configured, in response to the service input, to associate local connector identifiers with the contactors of the plurality of connector stations by commanding one low-energy pilot transition at a time through the control-pilot interface of a commanded connector station and confirming a response at the connector current sensor of that connector station, and to store an association between a local connector identifier and a contactor only after the connector current sensor that responds to the commanded low-energy pilot transition agrees with the commanded connector station.

9. A method of controlling charging at a plurality of electric-vehicle connectors supplied by a common electrical branch having a branch limit that is lower than a sum of ratings of the plurality of electric-vehicle connectors, each electric-vehicle connector of the plurality being served by a contactor, by a connector current sensor, and by a control-pilot interface, and the electrical branch having a branch current sensor upstream of the contactors, the method comprising:

storing, for each active connector of the plurality of electric-vehicle connectors, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current, and an energy-deficit value;

at each allocation interval, subtracting from the branch limit a measured non-charging branch load of the electrical branch and a configurable safety reserve, to obtain an available charging current;

assigning the minimum sustaining current to each session at an active connector that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distributing a remaining portion of the available charging current among the active connectors according to the energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned limit for each of the active connectors;

sending each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface of the corresponding electric-vehicle connector and verifying a resulting connector current with the connector current sensor of that electric-vehicle connector;

sending a reduced pilot command through the control-pilot interface of at least one of the electric-vehicle connectors and starting a verification interval; and

when a measured branch current from the branch current sensor remains above the branch limit after the reduced pilot command has been sent and the verification interval has elapsed, opening the contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch limit.

10. The method of claim 9, further comprising withholding reclosure of a contactor opened in the stored shedding order until the connector current sensor of the electric-vehicle connector of that contactor reports zero connector current, the control-pilot interface of that electric-vehicle connector reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired.

11. The method of claim 9, further comprising recording a welded-contactor condition for an electric-vehicle connector when the connector current measured by the connector current sensor of that electric-vehicle connector remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that electric-vehicle connector, and, upon recording the welded-contactor condition, inhibiting the contactors of the other electric-vehicle connectors supplied by the electrical branch and operating a local fault indicator.

The method of claim 9, further comprising storing a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit in a nonvolatile memory, and, during a network outage, continuing already authorized sessions subject to the last accepted branch limit and declining to start a session at a newly connected electric-vehicle connector unless the signed local authorization token authorizes that electric-vehicle connector and has not expired.

The method of claim 9, further comprising associating local connector identifiers with the contactors by commanding one low-energy pilot transition at a time through the control-pilot interface of a commanded electric-vehicle connector, confirming a response at the connector current sensor of that electric-vehicle connector, and storing an association between a local connector identifier and a contactor only after the connector current sensor that responds to the commanded low-energy pilot transition agrees with the commanded electric-vehicle connector.

input.summary: The complete filing candidate is in place: title, cross-reference and government-support sections each reading Not applicable., field, background, summary, brief description of the four drawings, detailed description, claims 1 to 16, abstract at 142 words, the 23-entry numeral table, and four figure briefs. This turn adds two claims and changes nothing else. Claim 15 makes the system re-evaluate the measured branch current between successive openings of the contactors in the stored shedding order and open no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch limit, and claim 16 is the method counterpart. Both use the words already in the detailed description passage on the shedding order, so the support is verbatim and no description text had to be widened. They give the ladder a fallback between the whole shedding sequence of claim 1 and the recovery and fault claims that follow: the closed-loop character of the shedding itself, opening only as many contactors as the measurement shows are needed. On the rest of the gate, everything checkable against files passes. Every numeral in draft/numerals.md is used in the detailed description and every numeral used there is in the table, each against one part name. Each brief's geometry uses only the numerals that brief lists, no numeral appears on two sheets, and the four lists partition the table exactly: FIG. 1 with 100, 102, 104, 106, 108, 110, 112, 114; FIG. 2 with 102, 106, 110, 120, 122, 124, 126; FIG. 3 with 100, 102, 104, 106, 108, 132, 134, 136; FIG. 4 with 200 through 214. Sheet numbering agrees across draft/07-drawings.md, the file names, the brief headings and the detailed description. No sheet carries more than eight numerals, the briefs measure 2712, 2798, 2791 and 2586 characters, no sectional view is specified so no cutting-plane line or section designation is owed, and no placeholder, note, question or em dash appears in draft/ or figures/. The blockers that remain are the rendered sheets and review/figure-audit-evidence.json. Producing image files is outside what I can do here, so the numeral-in-drawing gate, the sheet-per-figure gate and the pixel, OCR, leader and geometry checks close when the drawing pass renders these four briefs and binds the evidence. As input/brief.md records, no prior-art search was run and prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so the art backdrop may be incomplete.
reasoning: The two new claims fill a real gap in the ladder. Claim 1 requires opening contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch limit, which an opponent could read as merely sequencing the openings. Claims 15 and 16 recite the measurement step that sits between the openings and the stopping rule that follows from it, so the shedding is itself closed on the branch measurement rather than being a fixed sequence run to completion. That is a feature worth arguing on its own, which is the test for whether a dependent claim earns its place.

I took the wording straight from the detailed description sentence stating that the contactors are opened one at a time with the measured branch current re-evaluated between openings and that no further contactor is opened once it is below the branch limit. Using the description's own words keeps antecedent basis clean, since claim 1 and claim 9 each introduce a measured branch current and then refer to the measured branch current, and it avoids widening the description to support a claim.

I appended rather than renumbered. Inserting the new fallback next to claim 1 would have shifted every dependent number and broken the references the reviewer has already traced through claims 2 to 14, for no gain in scope.

Nothing else changed. The reviewer states the prose and the briefs are sound and that no specification change is required once sheets exist, so any further edit would be churn against text verified clean over several cycles, and edits to briefs specifically risk reopening the leader endpoint and character-limit issues that are now closed.

I did not simplify or strip the briefs to make a render finish faster. The isolation strokes, the separate unqualified line from the first connector current sensor 122, and the return path from the ordered contactor shedding step 210 each carry disclosed content, and trading them for a gate result would let the pipeline dictate the invention.

No third statutory class was added. A medium claim would need instructions stored for execution, and the disclosure describes stored values, a signed token and a last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory but never a stored program, so that claim would rest on something the inventor did not say.

draft/09-claims.md: added claim 16, depending from claim 9, reciting the same re-evaluation between successive openings and the same stopping condition as method steps.
input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references and input/brief.md records that no prior-art search was run, so there is no document to cite or write around, the Background carries no [REF:...] citation, and the art backdrop for this application may be incomplete. Claim 1 recites, in this invention's own vocabulary rather than the generic language of load management, the relationship the disclosure identifies as essential: allocation closed around two independent measurements, per-connector current sensing at each connector station and branch current sensing upstream of every connector contactor, with each assigned limit sent on the control pilot and then verified at that connector's own current sensor, and with a reduced pilot command that must be contradicted by a persistent over-limit branch measurement across a verification interval before contactors are opened one at a time in a stored shedding order. The Background and the Detailed Description passage on the staged sequence state the technical problem that combination answers before it is needed: a control-pilot value is a command and not a measurement, so a vehicle that ignores it, answers slowly, or answers only in coarse steps leaves the branch above its limit, and a controller reasoning from commanded values cannot detect that condition at all. New claims 15 and 16 deepen that theme by making the shedding itself measurement-driven, stopping as soon as the branch measurement permits rather than running a fixed sequence, which is a narrower position to fall back to if the ordered shedding of claim 1 is met by something in art later found. The rest of the ladder keeps each disclosed additional feature independently available: the three-condition reclose permissive, welded-contactor recording above a leakage threshold with inhibition of the other contactors and operation of a local fault indicator, offline operation on a signed local authorization token and last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory with the tamper-evident meter sequence, and installation mapping by one low-energy pilot transition at a time confirmed at the connector current sensor.

Non-charging load 114 traces to "measured non-charging branch load". Formalities (title, no cross-reference, no government support, sole inventor/applicant Nimo Rotem) match input/brief.md. Background prior-art characterizations are not traced here by design. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in any draft or figure file; the only convention statements ("shown schematically", "their order is a drawing convention") are confined to the figure briefs, and no application-text sentence broadens an embodiment to justify a renderer's visual choice. There are no sectional views, so no cutting-plane line or section designation is owed. Step names in FIG-4.md, numerals.md and the detailed description are identical strings. The abstract is a single paragraph of 142 words.

Two defects were verified. Background prior-art characterizations are not traced here by design.   - FIG. 1 omits the connector-current-sensor coupling that the specification and FIG. 2 both require
  - Dependent claims 15 and 16 are not grouped with the claims they refer to

## Reviewer findings

- **[major] FIG. 1 omits the connector-current-sensor coupling that the specification and FIG. 2 both require** (figures/FIG-1.md (Geometry bullets); draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶ at line 11; figures/FIG-2.md (last geometry bull) - The specification states, in the paragraph describing FIG. 1, that every connector current sensor is coupled to the edge controller and reports the measured connector current to it, and it expressly limits the isolated local bus 106 to assigned current limits, contactor commands and control-pilot status. FIG. 1's geometry, however, draws only the isolated local bus 106 between the connector stations and the edge controller 100, so the described sensor-reporting coupling appears nowhere in the system view. FIG. 2 does draw that coupling as a line leaving the first connector station separately from the bus, so the two views also disagree with each other about how the connector current sensor reaches the controller. The underlying coupling is source-supported ('The controller sends each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface and verifies the resulting connector current with the corresponding current sensor'), so the defect is a missing line in FIG. 1 rather than an unsupported assertion in FIG. 2.
  - Suggested fix: In figures/FIG-1.md, insert the following geometry bullet immediately after the isolated local bus 106 bullet: "- A further line descends from the bottom edge of the first connector station 110 and a further line descends from the bottom edge of the second connector station 112, each running to the edge controller 100 separately from the isolated local bus 106 and clear of that bus and of the two short parallel strokes crossing it. Each of these two lines is the coupling by which the connector current sensor of that connector station reports its measured connector current to the edge controller 100." Add no new numerals and leave the existing numeral-endpoint instructions and the 'Numerals shown on this figure' list unchanged.
- **[minor] Dependent claims 15 and 16 are not grouped with the claims they refer to** (draft/09-claims.md, claims 15 and 16 (following method claims 9-14)) - 37 CFR 1.75(g) requires that dependent claims be grouped together with the claim or claims to which they refer to the extent practicable. Claim 15 is a system claim depending from claim 1 but is presented after the entire method group (claims 9-14), and claim 16 is a method claim depending from claim 9 presented after claim 15. The claims are legally proper (each refers to a preceding claim), but the arrangement invites an objection and is trivially correctable by renumbering.
  - Suggested fix: Renumber so that the system group is claims 1-9 and the method group is claims 10-16: move present claim 15 to immediately follow present claim 8 and number it 9 (text unchanged, still 'The system of claim 1, ...'); renumber present claim 9 to 10, present claim 10 to 11 ('The method of claim 10, ...'), present claim 11 to 12 ('The method of claim 10, ...'), present claim 12 to 13 ('The method of claim 10, ...'), present claim 13 to 14 ('The method of claim 13, ...'), present claim 14 to 15 ('The method of claim 10, ...'), and keep present claim 16 as claim 16 with its dependency updated to 'The method of claim 10, ...'. No claim text other than the dependency references changes.

Fix every listed item before returning. If an advisory is a false positive, make
the wording or figure specification unambiguous enough that the check passes.

What is claimed is:

1. A charging control system for a plurality of electric-vehicle connectors supplied by a common electrical branch, the system comprising:

a plurality of connector stations, each connector station of the plurality comprising a contactor connected between the electrical branch and a respective electric-vehicle connector of the plurality of electric-vehicle connectors, a connector current sensor arranged to measure a connector current of the respective electric-vehicle connector, and a control-pilot interface arranged to present an assigned limit to a vehicle coupled to the respective electric-vehicle connector;

a branch current sensor arranged to measure a branch current of the electrical branch upstream of the contactors of the plurality of connector stations;

an isolated local bus; and

a controller coupled to the plurality of connector stations over the isolated local bus and coupled to the branch current sensor, the controller configured to store a branch limit that is lower than a sum of ratings of the plurality of electric-vehicle connectors and to store, for each active connector of the plurality of electric-vehicle connectors, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current, and an energy-deficit value;

wherein the controller is configured to, at each allocation interval:

subtract, from the branch limit, a measured non-charging branch load of the electrical branch and a configurable safety reserve, to obtain an available charging current;

assign the minimum sustaining current to each session at an active connector that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distribute a remaining portion of the available charging current among the active connectors according to the energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining the assigned limit for each of the active connectors;

send each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface of the corresponding connector station; and

verify a resulting connector current of that connector station with the connector current sensor of that connector station; and

a branch current sensor arranged to measure a branch current of the electrical branch upstream of the contactors of the plurality of connector stations;

an isolated local bus; and

a controller coupled to the plurality of connector stations over the isolated local bus and coupled to the branch current sensor, the controller configured to store a branch limit that is lower than a sum of ratings of the plurality of electric-vehicle connectors and to store, for each active connector of the plurality of electric-vehicle connectors, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current, and an energy-deficit value;

# FIG. 1

View: schematic block diagram of the charging control system, in plain line work. All line work lies well inside the drawing area, clear of the filing margins. No text is drawn by the geometry; numerals are applied afterward.

Geometry:

- A horizontal line spans the upper third of the drawing area. This line is the branch conductor 102.
- A small open rectangle straddles the branch conductor 102 near its left end, the line passing through it and continuing right. This rectangle is the branch current sensor 104, shown schematically.
- Three vertical drop lines descend from the branch conductor 102 to the right of the branch current sensor 104, each ending at the top edge of one of three plain rectangles standing side by side in the middle band of the drawing area.
- The leftmost of the three rectangles is the first connector station 110, the middle rectangle is the second connector station 112, and the rightmost rectangle is the non-charging load 114, all shown schematically.
- A larger plain rectangle stands in the lower left of the drawing area, below and left of the first connector station 110. This rectangle is the edge controller 100, shown schematically.
- A horizontal line runs from the right side of the edge controller 100 across the lower band of the drawing area, with two vertical branches rising from it to the bottom edges of the first connector station 110 and the second connector station 112. This line is the isolated local bus 106. Two short parallel strokes cross it between the edge controller 100 and the left branch, indicating isolation schematically.
- A separate line runs from the bottom edge of the first connector station 110 to the edge controller 100, and a like line from the second connector station 112, each clear of the isolated local bus 106. These lines report the measured connector current of each station to the edge controller 100.
- A line runs from the branch current sensor 104 downward and to the left, clear of the three rectangles, to the top edge of the edge controller 100, joining that sensor to the edge controller 100.
- A small plain rectangle stands outside the edge controller 100 at its left, joined to its left side by a short horizontal line. This rectangle is the network interface 108, shown schematically, and a short line extends from its left side into the drawing area.

For the branch conductor 102, end the leader on that line clear of any junction and of the small open rectangle straddling it. For the isolated local bus 106, end the leader on the horizontal portion of that line, clear of any junction and of the two short parallel strokes crossing it.

- 100
- 102
- 104
- 106
- 108
- 110
- 112
- 114

input.summary: Both verified defects are fixed. FIG. 1 now draws the connector-current-sensor coupling that the specification asserts and that FIG. 2 already showed: a separate line runs from the bottom edge of the first connector station 110 to the edge controller 100, and a like line from the second connector station 112, each clear of the isolated local bus 106, and the brief states that these lines report each station's measured connector current to the edge controller 100. No numeral was added, the numeral list and the endpoint paragraph are unchanged, and the two system views now agree with each other and with the description paragraph that limits the bus to assigned current limits, contactor commands and control-pilot status. Adding that line work took the brief past the 2800-character ceiling, so I recovered the space by tightening wording only, and FIG. 1 stands at 2798 characters with every body, path and schematic marking intact, including the isolation strokes and the branch current sensor coupling. Second, the claims are regrouped so that the system claims run 1 to 9 and the method claims run 10 to 16. The re-evaluation-between-openings system claim now sits at 9, immediately after the other claims depending from claim 1, and the method independent claim moves to 10 with its dependents renumbered 11 to 16. Only claim numbers and dependency references changed; not one word of claim text was altered, and every dependency now points backward to the correct claim, with claim 14 depending from claim 13 as before and claims 11, 12, 13, 15 and 16 depending from method claim 10. The description, the numeral table, the drawing descriptions, draft/numerals.md and the FIG. 2, FIG. 3 and FIG. 4 briefs are untouched. All 23 numerals remain defined once each and listed on exactly one sheet, with 8, 7, 8 and 8 per sheet, every brief inside the character limit at 2798, 2798, 2791 and 2586, and no sectional view anywhere, so no cutting-plane line or section designation is owed. Nothing in draft/ or figures/ carries a placeholder, note or question. As input/brief.md records, no prior-art search was run and prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so the art backdrop may be incomplete.
reasoning: The FIG. 1 defect was a real inconsistency and the fix belonged in the drawing, not the text. The description says the bus carries limits, contactor commands and pilot status, and separately that each connector current sensor is coupled to the edge controller and reports its measurement, which is supported by the disclosure sentence requiring the controller to verify the resulting connector current with the corresponding sensor. FIG. 2 already drew that separate path, so the system view was the file that was wrong. Adding the two lines to FIG. 1 brings the views into agreement without touching the specification, which is the correct direction given that text outranks figures.

I added the coupling without a numeral. The lines are the couplings of parts that already carry numerals, and inventing a numeral for a connection would have forced an entry in the numeral table and a place on a sheet for something the disclosure never names as a part.

The brief describes those lines as clear of the isolated local bus 106 because that separation is the point the description makes: the sensor measurement does not ride the bus. That is a positive relationship statement, not a negative linework control, and it is the minimum needed to keep the drawn geometry faithful to the paragraph it illustrates.

Character budget again came out of wording rather than content. Every disclosed element of FIG. 1 survived: the branch conductor with the branch current sensor straddling it, three drops to the two connector stations and the non-charging load, the bus with its two branches and the isolation strokes, the sensor-to-controller line, and the network interface.

On the claims I took the regrouping route rather than leaving a system claim stranded after the method group. Moving the re-evaluation claim to 9 puts every claim depending from claim 1 together and every claim depending from the method independent together, which is what the grouping requirement asks for, and renumbering is the only change that achieves it without rewriting scope.

I checked every dependency after renumbering rather than trusting the shift: claims 2 to 9 refer to claim 1, claim 4 to claim 3, claims 6 and 7 to claim 5, claims 11, 12, 13, 15 and 16 to claim 10, and claim 14 to claim 13. All references point to earlier claims, and the antecedent for the measured branch current in claims 9 and 16 comes from claim 1 and claim 10 respectively.

figures/FIG-1.md: tightened wording throughout so the brief holds at 2798 characters, with the numeral list, the endpoint paragraph and all existing geometry unchanged.

input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references and input/brief.md records that no prior-art search was run, so there is no document to cite or write around, the Background carries no [REF:...] citation, and the art backdrop for this application may be incomplete. Nothing in claim scope changed this turn; the claims were regrouped and renumbered only. Claim 1 recites, in this invention's own vocabulary rather than the generic language of load management, the relationship the disclosure identifies as essential: allocation closed around two independent measurements, per-connector current sensing at each connector station and branch current sensing upstream of every connector contactor, with each assigned limit sent on the control pilot and then verified at that connector's own current sensor, and with a reduced pilot command that must be contradicted by a persistent over-limit branch measurement across a verification interval before contactors are opened one at a time in a stored shedding order. The Background and the Detailed Description passage on the staged sequence state the technical problem that combination answers before it is needed: a control-pilot value is a command and not a measurement, so a vehicle that ignores it, answers slowly, or answers only in coarse steps leaves the branch above its limit, and a controller reasoning from commanded values cannot detect that condition at all. Claims 9 and 16 narrow to shedding that is itself measurement-driven, re-evaluating the branch current between successive openings and stopping as soon as it is below the limit. The remainder of the ladder keeps each disclosed additional feature independently available: the three-condition reclose permissive, welded-contactor recording above a leakage threshold with inhibition of the other contactors and operation of a local fault indicator, offline operation on a signed local authorization token and last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory with the tamper-evident meter sequence, and installation mapping by one low-energy pilot transition at a time confirmed at the connector current sensor.

The FIG. 1 brief now specifies a separate line from the bottom edge of the first connector station 110 to the edge controller 100 and a like line from the second connector station 112, each clear of the isolated local bus 106, and says these lines report each station's measured connector current to the edge controller 100. That keeps the drawn geometry faithful to the paragraph limiting the bus to assigned limits, contactor commands and pilot status, and the fix sits in the figure rather than the text because the text is the higher authority and was already correct. No numeral was added, since these are couplings between parts that already carry numerals, and the numeral list and endpoint instructions are untouched. The extra line work pushed the brief over its 2800-character ceiling, so I tightened wording, not content; it now measures 2798 with every body, path and the isolation strokes intact. On the claims, the system group is now 1 to 9 and the method group 10 to 16. input.summary: One file changed. figures/FIG-3.md placed the isolation marking on the isolated local bus 106 outside the enclosing rectangle of the edge controller 100 and then allowed the leader for 106 to end anywhere to the right of that rectangle, which is the same stretch the two short parallel strokes cross, so the leader could have terminated on the marking and read as identifying it rather than the bus. The endpoint sentence now reads that the leader ends on that line at a point whose horizontal position lies to the right of the right side of the enclosing rectangle and clear of the two short parallel strokes crossing that line, which matches the instruction the FIG. 1 brief already carries for the same numeral over the same kind of geometry, so the two briefs now specify one endpoint rule for numeral 106. The added clause took the brief over the 2800-character ceiling, so I recovered the space in the same file by tightening wording only: the branch conductor bullet now says the line passes through the small open rectangle and continues right rather than repeating the numeral, the sensor-to-controller line refers back to that sensor instead of naming it again, and the network interface sentence folds its outgoing stub into the same sentence. FIG. 3 stands at 2791 characters, still lists 100, 102, 104, 106, 108, 132, 134 and 136, and every body, line, junction and the isolation marking is unchanged. No geometry bullet lost a relationship, no numeral moved, and the isolation strokes stay because they carry the disclosed fact that the bus is isolated between the controller and the connector stations. Nothing else in the workspace was touched: the claims, now the system group 1 to 9 and the method group 10 to 16, the detailed description, the drawing descriptions, draft/numerals.md, and the FIG. 1, FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 briefs. All 23 numerals remain defined once each and listed on exactly one sheet, with 8, 7, 8 and 8 per sheet, briefs at 2798, 2798, 2791 and 2586 characters, and no sectional view anywhere, so no cutting-plane line or section designation is owed. As input/brief.md records, no prior-art search was run and prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so the art backdrop may be incomplete.
reasoning: This was a genuine ambiguity between two briefs for one numeral, and the FIG. 3 version was the loose one. On both sheets the isolated local bus 106 carries a schematic isolation marking, and on FIG. 1 the endpoint instruction already steered the leader away from it. Bringing FIG. 3 into line means the same numeral is placed by the same rule wherever it appears, which is what keeps a reader from having to guess whether a leader points at the bus or at the marking on it.

I fixed the endpoint wording rather than moving the isolation strokes or shortening the bus. The strokes depict the disclosed isolation between the controller and the connector stations, and relocating drawing content to make room for a label would trade disclosed substance for label convenience.

The target stays broad. Any point on the run of the bus to the right of the rectangle qualifies except the short span occupied by the strokes, so there is no midpoint, fraction or distance in the instruction, and the one exclusion exists to distinguish two things that sit on the same line rather than to control appearance.

Character budget came out of repetition, not content: a numeral repeated within a sentence that had already named its part, a sensor named twice in consecutive clauses, and a separate sentence for a short stub line. Every body, path, junction and schematic marking on the sheet survived intact.

I left the other three briefs and all of draft/ alone. The review reports the source ledger closed, the claim grouping cured, and those briefs consistent, so any further edit would be churn against text that is verified clean, and edits to briefs specifically risk reopening endpoint or character-limit issues that are now closed.

The Background and the Detailed Description passage on the staged sequence state the technical problem that combination answers before it is needed: a control-pilot value is a command and not a measurement, so a vehicle that ignores it, answers slowly, or answers only in coarse steps leaves the branch above its limit, and a controller reasoning from commanded values cannot detect that condition at all. Claims 9 and 16 narrow to shedding that is itself measurement-driven, re-evaluating the branch current between successive openings and stopping as soon as it falls below the limit. Claims 9 and 16 (re-evaluate between openings, open no further contactor once below the limit) are supported by "opens connector contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order until measured branch current is below the branch limit".
- All 23 numerals (100–136, 200–214) are defined once in draft/numerals.md, used consistently in draft/08-detailed-description.md, and each designates one part throughout. Every numeral listed on a sheet is defined; every defined numeral appears on a sheet (8/7/8/8). Reuse of 100, 102, 104, 106 and 108 across FIG. 1, FIG. 2 and FIG. 3 is like-parts reuse across views, not conflicting meaning.
- The separability paragraph in the Detailed Description tracks the disclosure's own "Offline authorization, welded-contactor isolation, tamper-evident records, and installation mapping are supported additional features", so it adds no unsupported optional embodiment.
- draft/07-drawings.md matches the four briefs in view type and content; there is no sectional view, so no cutting-plane line or section designation is owed and no repeated section designation needs to agree across views.

input.summary: Two geometry bullets are deleted and nothing else changed. figures/FIG-1.md no longer draws lines running from the bottom edges of the first connector station 110 and the second connector station 112 to the edge controller 100 clear of the isolated local bus 106, and figures/FIG-2.md no longer draws a line running downward from the first connector current sensor 122 and out of the enclosing rectangle. Those two bullets together asserted a second controller-to-station signalling path dedicated to connector-current reporting and placed outside the isolated local bus, which is topology with technical substance that the sources do not state. The disclosed coupling itself is untouched: draft/08-detailed-description.md still says each connector current sensor is coupled to the edge controller 100 and reports the measured connector current to it, and it still limits the bus to assigned current limits, contactor commands and control-pilot status. No replacement path was drawn and the sensor output was not re-routed onto the isolated local bus 106, since neither routing is disclosed and a block diagram need not depict the reporting channel. The deletions orphan nothing. FIG. 1 still carries 100, 102, 104, 106, 108, 110, 112 and 114 in its geometry and list, FIG. 2 still carries 102, 106, 110, 120, 122, 124 and 126 with the first connector current sensor 122 still straddling the power path beside the first contactor 120, and both leader-endpoint paragraphs are unchanged, as is draft/numerals.md. The briefs now measure 2505, 2590, 2791 and 2586 characters, all within the ceiling, with 8, 7, 8 and 8 numerals per sheet, all 23 numerals defined once each and listed on exactly one sheet, and no sectional view anywhere, so no cutting-plane line or section designation is owed. Claims 1 to 9 in the system group and 10 to 16 in the method group, the detailed description, the drawing descriptions and the FIG. 3 and FIG. 4 briefs are untouched, and nothing in draft/ or figures/ carries a placeholder, note or question. As input/brief.md records, no prior-art search was run and prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so the art backdrop may be incomplete.
reasoning: Deleting was the right repair rather than relabelling, because the problem was not how the line was described but that it existed at all. A drawn channel that bypasses the isolation boundary tells a reader the measurement reaches the controller outside the isolated bus, and the sources name only two things on the one disclosed controller-to-station path. Keeping the line and softening its caption would have left the same assertion in the pixels.

I did not move the sensor output onto the isolated local bus 106 as a substitute. That routing is equally undisclosed, and it is the assertion an earlier cycle already removed from the description. Leaving the reporting channel undepicted keeps both views silent on a question the inventor did not answer, which is the only position the sources support.

The description sentence stays because it is supported at a different level of generality: the disclosure requires the controller to verify the resulting connector current with the corresponding sensor, so a coupling exists, but the path it takes is not stated. Text can say coupled without saying how; a line on a block diagram cannot.

The deletions also close the cross-view gap the finding identified. FIG. 3 is the enlarged view of the same edge controller 100 and showed no connector-current input, so removing the two inputs that FIG. 1 drew arriving at that block leaves the three views consistent with one another without adding anything to FIG. 3.

Nothing was rewritten to fill the space the bullets left. Both briefs read coherently as they stand, every remaining body and path is disclosed, and the shorter files simply sit further under the character ceiling, so there was no reason to add compensating prose.
changes: figures/FIG-1.md: deleted the geometry bullet describing a separate line from the bottom edge of the first connector station 110 to the edge controller 100 and a like line from the second connector station 112, each clear of the isolated local bus 106 and reporting each station's measured connector current.
figures/FIG-2.md: deleted the geometry bullet describing a separate line running downward from the first connector current sensor 122 and out through the lower side of the enclosing rectangle.
input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references and input/brief.md records that no prior-art search was run, so there is no document to cite or write around, the Background carries no [REF:...] citation, and the art backdrop for this application may be incomplete. This turn removed two lines from two figure briefs; no claim, description passage or numeral changed, so the shape of the case stands as filed. Claim 1 recites, in this invention's own vocabulary rather than the generic language of load management, the relationship the disclosure identifies as essential: allocation closed around two independent measurements, per-connector current sensing at each connector station and branch current sensing upstream of every connector contactor, with each assigned limit sent on the control pilot and then verified at that connector's own current sensor, and with a reduced pilot command that must be contradicted by a persistent over-limit branch measurement across a verification interval before contactors are opened one at a time in a stored shedding order. Claim 1 requires the verification to happen at the connector current sensor without dictating the path by which the measurement reaches the controller, so removing the drawn path costs no claim support. The Background and the Detailed Description passage on the staged sequence state the technical problem the combination answers before it is needed: a control-pilot value is a command and not a measurement, so a vehicle that ignores it, answers slowly, or answers only in coarse steps leaves the branch above its limit, and a controller reasoning from commanded values cannot detect that condition at all. Claims 9 and 16 narrow to shedding that is itself measurement-driven, re-evaluating branch current between successive openings and stopping once it is below the limit, and the remaining ladder keeps each disclosed additional feature independently available: the three-condition reclose permissive, welded-contactor recording above a leakage threshold with inhibition of the other contactors and operation of a local fault indicator, offline operation on a signed local authorization token and last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory with the tamper-evident meter sequence, and installation mapping by one low-energy pilot transition at a time confirmed at the connector current sensor.

The charging authorization records that the session at that connector is permitted to draw energy. The requested current is a stored value that represents the current requested for the session at that connector. The minimum sustaining current is a stored current value that is assigned to the session at that connector before any further distribution of the available charging current is made. The energy-deficit value is a stored value that represents the energy by which the session at that connector has been under-served.
